title: Diego Suarez Bay And Ramena Coast
summary: Turquoise lagoons, red sandstone canyons and wild bays at the northern tip of Madagascar.
tip: From June to September the varatraza trade wind blows hard on the bay: perfect for kitesurfers, a little choppy for boat trips.
overview: Diego Suarez sits on one of the largest natural bays in the world. In six relaxed days you sail to the Emerald Sea, walk among the Red Tsingy and drive along the Three Bays, with time left for long lunches of grilled fish on the beach.
Nights are spent between the colonial town of Diego and the fishing village of Ramena, so every morning starts close to the water.
highlights: Sail across the Emerald Sea and swim in its shallow turquoise water
Walk among the Red Tsingy, sharp pinnacles shaped by erosion
Drive the coastal track of the Three Bays: Sakalava, Pigeons and Dunes
Spot crowned lemurs and chameleons in Amber Mountain National Park

itinerary.title: Arrival in Diego Suarez
itinerary.text: Welcome at Arrachart airport and transfer to your hotel. Late afternoon walk in the old colonial town, then sunset over the bay and the Sugar Loaf island of Nosy Lonjo.

itinerary.title: The Red Tsingy
itinerary.text: A morning drive south to the Red Tsingy, a canyon of red and ochre pinnacles that glow in the low light. Back in town for a free afternoon.

itinerary.title: Ramena and the Emerald Sea
itinerary.text: Transfer to Ramena, then a sailing boat crosses the bay to the Emerald Sea. Swim, snorkel and enjoy a seafood lunch on a sandy islet.

itinerary.title: The Three Bays
itinerary.text: A 4x4 track follows the coast to Sakalava Bay, Pigeons Bay and Dunes Bay. Short walks to the Cap Miné lighthouse and plenty of time to swim.

itinerary.title: Amber Mountain National Park
itinerary.text: A cool rainforest on an old volcano: waterfalls, crater lakes, crowned lemurs and some of the smallest chameleons on Earth.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.text: Free morning for a last coffee by the bay, then transfer to the airport for your flight.

title: Nosy Be, Nosy Komba And Nosy Iranja
stops: Nosy Be · Nosy Komba · Nosy Iranja
summary: Island hopping between perfumed Nosy Be, lemur-filled Nosy Komba and the twin islands of Nosy Iranja.
tip: Whale sharks visit the waters around Nosy Be from October to December, humpback whales from July to September.
overview: Nosy Be smells of ylang-ylang and vanilla. From there, small boats take you to the islands around it: Nosy Komba and its friendly black lemurs, the marine reserve of Nosy Tanikely, and Nosy Iranja, two islands joined by a long sandbar at low tide.
The pace is slow on purpose. Mornings at sea, afternoons on the beach, and one night on Nosy Iranja to enjoy it after the day visitors leave.
highlights: Walk the sandbar between the two islands of Nosy Iranja at low tide
Snorkel with turtles in the marine reserve of Nosy Tanikely
Meet black lemurs in the forest of Nosy Komba
Watch the sunset over the bay from the top of Mont Passot
included: Private vehicle with an experienced driver
English or French speaking local guide
National park entrance fees and local guides
Accommodation in double room
7 nights in beach hotels
Breakfast every day, lunch on boat days
All boat transfers between the islands

itinerary.title: Arrival in Nosy Be
itinerary.text: Welcome at Fascene airport and transfer to your beach hotel. The rest of the day is yours.

itinerary.title: Lokobe forest by pirogue
itinerary.text: Paddle a traditional outrigger canoe to the edge of Lokobe, the last primary forest of Nosy Be, home to black lemurs and panther chameleons.

itinerary.title: Nosy Komba and Nosy Tanikely
itinerary.text: Morning on Nosy Komba with its lemurs and embroidery village, then snorkelling in the clear water of the Nosy Tanikely marine reserve.

itinerary.title: Nosy Iranja
itinerary.text: Boat ride south to Nosy Iranja. Walk the sandbar, swim, and spend the night on the island. Green and hawksbill turtles nest on its beaches.

itinerary.title: Ylang-ylang and Mont Passot
itinerary.text: Back to Nosy Be. Visit an ylang-ylang distillery and the sacred fig tree of Mahatsinjo, then sunset over the crater lakes from Mont Passot.

itinerary.title: Free day
itinerary.text: Rest on the beach, or add a dive. From October to December, ask us about a whale shark trip.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.text: Transfer to Fascene airport for your flight.

title: Ambanja Cocoa Country And Northern Wildlife
summary: From the cocoa plantations of the Sambirano valley to the grey tsingy of Ankarana.
tip: Some trails in Ankarana close during the rainy season, from January to March.
overview: The Sambirano valley around Ambanja grows some of the finest cocoa in the world. You walk the plantations with the farmers, then follow the road north to the limestone massif of Ankarana, its caves and its suspension bridge over the tsingy.
The circuit ends in Diego Suarez with the rainforest of Amber Mountain and a day at sea, crossing the whole north of the island by road.
highlights: Follow cocoa from the tree to the bean in a Sambirano plantation
Cross the suspension bridge above the grey tsingy of Ankarana
Explore caves and underground rivers with a park guide
Look for crowned lemurs and leaf-tailed geckos at night

English or French speaking local guide
National park entrance fees and local guides

itinerary.title: Arrival and crossing to the mainland
itinerary.text: Welcome in Nosy Be, then a short boat ride to Ankify and the road to Ambanja.

itinerary.title: The Sambirano valley
itinerary.text: Two days among cocoa, vanilla, pepper and ylang-ylang plantations. Taste fresh cocoa pulp and learn how the beans are fermented and dried.

itinerary.title: North to Ankarana
itinerary.text: A long scenic drive on the RN6 through villages and rice fields, arriving at the edge of Ankarana National Park.

itinerary.title: Ankarana National Park
itinerary.text: Hikes to the grey tsingy and the suspension bridge, the Lost River and the bat caves. Night walk to find mouse lemurs and geckos.

itinerary.title: Red Tsingy and Diego Suarez
itinerary.text: On the way to Diego Suarez, stop at the Red Tsingy, then settle in the colonial town by the bay.

itinerary.title: Amber Mountain National Park
itinerary.text: Waterfalls, crater lakes and cool rainforest, home to crowned lemurs and tiny chameleons.

itinerary.title: The Emerald Sea
itinerary.text: Sailing day from Ramena to the turquoise lagoon of the Emerald Sea, with swimming and lunch on the beach.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.text: Transfer to Arrachart airport for your flight.

title: Antananarivo And The Royal Highlands
summary: Royal hills, rice terraces and artisan towns in the heart of Madagascar.
bestTime: All year, best from April to November
tip: The highlands are cool: nights can drop below 10 °C from June to August. Bring a warm layer.
overview: The highlands are where the Merina kingdom was born. You climb to the royal palaces of Antananarivo and the sacred hill of Ambohimanga, then drive south along the RN7 through rice terraces to Antsirabe, the town of pousse-pousse and craftsmen.
A short circuit, perfect at the start or the end of a longer trip.
highlights: Visit the Rova, the Queen’s palace above Antananarivo
Walk the sacred royal hill of Ambohimanga, a UNESCO World Heritage site
Watch aluminium pots being cast by hand in Ambatolampy
Ride a pousse-pousse in Antsirabe and hike to the crater lake of Tritriva
included: Private vehicle with an experienced driver
English or French speaking local guide
National park entrance fees and local guides

4 nights in hotels

itinerary.title: Arrival in Antananarivo
itinerary.text: Welcome at Ivato airport and transfer to your hotel. Short walk in the upper town if the flight allows.

itinerary.title: Royal Antananarivo and Ambohimanga
itinerary.text: Morning at the Rova and the upper town, then the royal hill of Ambohimanga, its wooden palace and its views over the rice fields.

itinerary.title: South on the RN7
itinerary.text: Drive through the highlands to Antsirabe, with a stop in Ambatolampy to meet the pot makers.

itinerary.title: Antsirabe and Lake Tritriva
itinerary.text: Pousse-pousse tour of the spa town, visits to gem cutters and horn carvers, then a walk around the deep green crater lake of Tritriva.

itinerary.title: Back to Antananarivo
itinerary.text: Return drive to the capital, a last stop at the craft market of La Digue, and transfer to the airport.

title: Baobab Avenue And The Tsingy
summary: The great baobabs of Morondava and the stone forest of the Tsingy de Bemaraha.
tip: The Tsingy de Bemaraha park and the tracks to reach it are closed during the rainy season, roughly from December to April.
overview: The west of Madagascar is a land of giants. Sunset on the Avenue of the Baobabs, then a 4x4 expedition north, across rivers on small ferries, to the Tsingy de Bemaraha, a forest of limestone needles listed by UNESCO.
It is an adventure: long days on dirt tracks, rewarded by some of the most striking landscapes on the island and quiet days by the sea in Morondava at the end.
highlights: Watch the sun set behind the Avenue of the Baobabs
Climb ladders and cross rope bridges in the Great Tsingy
Paddle through the gorges of the Manambolo river
Look for the fossa during a walk in Kirindy forest

itinerary.title: Arrival in Antananarivo
itinerary.text: Welcome at Ivato airport and transfer to your hotel.

itinerary.title: Flight to Morondava
itinerary.text: Short flight to the west coast. In the late afternoon, the Avenue of the Baobabs at sunset.

itinerary.title: Kirindy forest
itinerary.text: Dry forest walks to look for the fossa, Verreaux’s sifakas and the giant jumping rat, then a night walk for mouse lemurs.

itinerary.title: North to Bekopaka
itinerary.text: A full day by 4x4, crossing the Tsiribihina river by ferry at Belo-sur-Tsiribihina, to reach Bekopaka at the gates of the Tsingy.

itinerary.title: The Great Tsingy
itinerary.text: Harness, ladders and rope bridges: a guided via ferrata in the heart of the stone forest.

itinerary.title: Small Tsingy and Manambolo gorges
itinerary.text: Easier trails in the Small Tsingy, then a pirogue ride through the gorges of the Manambolo river.

itinerary.title: Back to Morondava
itinerary.text: The long road south, with a stop at the twisted Baobabs in Love.

itinerary.title: Morondava by the sea
itinerary.text: Rest on the beach and cross by pirogue to the fishing village of Betania.

itinerary.title: Flight to Antananarivo
itinerary.text: Morning flight back to the capital, afternoon free.

itinerary.title: Royal hill of Ambohimanga
itinerary.text: Half day at the sacred hill of Ambohimanga, then a last shopping stop at the craft market.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.text: Transfer to Ivato airport for your flight.

title: Rainforests, Lemurs And Indri Trails
summary: The song of the indri, the island of Sainte-Marie and the wild peninsula of Masoala.
tip: The east coast is the wettest part of Madagascar. Bring a light rain jacket whatever the season, and quick-dry clothes for Masoala.
overview: The east is Madagascar at its greenest. In Andasibe you wake up to the call of the indri, the largest living lemur. On Ile Sainte-Marie you rest on quiet beaches and, in season, watch humpback whales from the shore.
The journey ends on the Masoala peninsula, where the rainforest runs down to the sea. Remote and rainy, it is one of the richest places for wildlife on the island.
highlights: Hear the indri sing at dawn in Andasibe
Watch humpback whales off Ile Sainte-Marie from July to September
Look for the red ruffed lemur, found only on Masoala
Kayak and snorkel in the marine park of Masoala

itinerary.title: Arrival in Antananarivo
itinerary.text: Welcome at Ivato airport and transfer to your hotel.

itinerary.title: Road to Andasibe
itinerary.text: About four hours east, from the highlands down into the rainforest. First night walk to find chameleons and frogs.

itinerary.title: The indri of Analamazaotra
itinerary.text: Early morning walk to find a family of indri and hear their song, the loudest call of any lemur.

itinerary.title: Mantadia National Park
itinerary.text: A wilder forest with longer trails, waterfalls and the colourful diademed sifaka.

itinerary.title: Back to Antananarivo
itinerary.text: Return drive to the capital to catch the next morning’s flight.

itinerary.title: Flight to Ile Sainte-Marie
itinerary.text: A short flight to the island, and the afternoon on the beach.

itinerary.title: Ile Sainte-Marie
itinerary.text: The pirate cemetery, a boat trip to Ile aux Nattes and, in season, whale watching with a certified operator.

itinerary.title: To Maroantsetra and Masoala
itinerary.text: Flight to Maroantsetra, then a boat across the bay of Antongil to your lodge on the peninsula.

itinerary.title: Masoala National Park
itinerary.text: Guided rainforest hikes for red ruffed lemurs and leaf-tailed geckos, kayaking along the coast and snorkelling in the marine park.

itinerary.title: Back to Antananarivo
itinerary.text: Boat to Maroantsetra and flight to the capital.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.text: Transfer to Ivato airport for your flight.
